Area Forecast Discussion

FXUS66 KSGX 221149
AFDSGX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Diego CA
449 AM PDT Thu Oct 22 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Showers and a slight chance of thunderstorms will continue
through today. There will be additional, mostly light showers for
tonight, decreasing and ending from northwest late Friday
afternoon. Southwest to west winds along the desert slopes of the
mountains will gust to 40 to 50 mph through this afternoon. It
will be dry and warmer for the weekend through Monday, then
gradually cooler for next week with a chance of precipitation for
late next week. Tides will increase over the weekend, remaining
elevated through much of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO
COUNTIES...

...UPDATED AVIATION DISCUSSION...

.SHORT TERM (Today through Saturday)...
Rainfall that has occurred across southwestern California since
Wednesday afternoon through midnight has been from bands of
showers with rainfall quite variable from the coast to the
mountains. Some locations have received less than 0.10 inch of
rainfall. A lot of areas have had 0.25 inch or less with the
generally wetter locations receiving 0.50 to 1 inch. The greatest
concentration of heavier amounts has been in the western San
Bernardino Mountains in the area around Lake Arrowhead with 1.5 to
2 inches with one report exceeding 3 inches.

Southwest winds have gusted to 45 to 55 mph, mostly along the
desert slopes of the San Bernardino County Mountains. Southwest to
west winds along the desert slopes of the mountains from the San
Bernardino Mountains southwest are expected for this morning
through this afternoon with gusts to 45 to 55 mph.

The upper low centered near Point Conception around sunrise today
is expected to move toward the northeast and into Nevada this
evening. A shortwave moving southward on the west side of the low
pressure system is expected to develop into a closed low pressure
system centered over southern California late Friday afternoon.
This low pressure system will gradually weaken and move toward the
east and northeast through the weekend.

Bands of showers with a slight chance of thunderstorms will
continue to move inland into southwestern California today. There
could be a decrease in showers for early this evening with
scattered showers from the west and northwest moving into
southwestern California from the west and northwest for later in
the evening and overnight. Showers are expected to continue into
Friday morning and end from the northwest during Friday afternoon.
Dry weather is expected for the weekend.

Additional rainfall for today through Friday for the coast to the
mountains of 0.25 to 0.50 is possible. Chances for 0.50 inch or
more of rainfall for the coast and valleys is generally 10 to 20
percent with 45 to 55 percent for the San Bernardino Mountains and
30 to 40 percent for the San Diego County mountains.

High temperatures for today will be as much as 10 to 15 degrees
cooler than Wednesday for the mountains and inland valleys with
high temperatures in the mountains 15 to 20 degrees below average.
High temperatures for today will be mostly in the 60s to around 70
for the coast and valleys and for the mountains in the 40s and
50s. High temperatures on Friday will be a few degrees warmer for
the coast to the mountains with greater warming of 5 to 10 degrees
on Saturday. High temperatures on Saturday will be as much as 5 to
10 degrees below average for the mountains. High temperatures on
Saturday will be mostly in the 70s for the coast and valleys and
in the 50s and 60s for the mountains with the lower deserts in
the lower to mid 80s.

&&

.LONG TERM (Sunday through Wednesday)...
High temperatures for Sunday will be a few to around 5 degrees
warmer, mostly in the mid 70s to lower 80s for the coast and
valleys, with coastal areas a few degrees warmer on Monday with
high temperatures for the coast and valleys in the mid 70s to mid
80s. Cooling will begin to spread inland on Wednesday with high
temperatures a few degrees cooler.

&&

.AVIATION...
221130Z...SCT SHRA and isolated TSRA this morning, decreasing in
frequency after 15Z, but continuing through about 22Z. Cigs down to
1500-2500 feet MSL and vis 3-5SM at times through 16Z, such as in
heavier SHRA or TSRA, otherwise bases will be 3500-4500 feet MSL.
Partial obscuration of mountains this morning, but improving vis
during the day. Isolated -SHRA after 22Z. Onshore winds in mountains
into deserts 25-30 kts, creating MOD up/downdrafts in lee of ridges.

&&

.MARINE...
A storm system will slowly move through the coastal waters today
through Friday. There is a slight chance of thunderstorms today. Any
thunderstorm is capable of producing gusty, erratic winds, choppy
seas, lightning, briefly heavy rainfall with reduced visibility, and
waterspouts. Isolated northwest wind gusts will occasionally exceed
20 knots Friday. No hazardous marine conditions are expected Friday
night through Monday.

&&

.BEACHES...
Astronomical high tides will create minor to moderate coastal
flooding starting Saturday. Tides are 1.4-1.6 feet above
predictions. Morning high tides could reach 7 feet Saturday morning
and are likely to exceed 7.5 feet by Monday morning.

&&

.SKYWARN...
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.

&&

.SGX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
CA...Wind Advisory until 6 PM PDT this evening for San Bernardino
     County Mountains.

     Wind Advisory until 6 PM PDT this evening for Riverside County
     Mountains-San Diego County Deserts-San Diego County
     Mountains-San Gorgonio Pass near Banning.

     Wind Advisory until 6 AM PDT early this morning for Apple and
     Lucerne Valleys.

PZ...None.
